mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the risk-free rate and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in < 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 0.5%, it signals a highly accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower discount rates and increased risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and fall in housing starts (HOUST) signals a deteriorating economic outlook, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months AND HOUST falls > 5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 7.0%), the economy is in a recessionary regime, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings and risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of instances when UNRATE > 7.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High consumer credit demand (RSAFS > 300,000 million dollars) indicates robust consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in < 60% of instances when RSAFS > 300000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% monthly growth signals accelerating inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to central bank tightening expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and inflation is accelerating (CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% monthly), it signals a risk of uncontrolled inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the central bank may be forced to tighten aggressively.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the quarterly GDP growth rate (from GDPC1) is above 2% but declining, it indicates a late-cycle expansion phase, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to the risk of a policy tightening and slowing growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of instances when GDP growth rate is above 2% and declining, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
